datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: TECP data shown in this manuscript
datasets.instrument_sensor: Thermal and Electrical Conductivity Probe (TECP) relative humidity (RH) sensor
datasets.measurement_observable: In situ atmospheric relative humidity (RH), frost point temperature (Tf), water vapor pressure (e), and associated TECP raw RH output (DNRH) and board temperature (Tb) used for recalibration/application
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ environmental time-series measurements (humidity sensor)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Sol 1 (Ls ~77°) to sol 150 (Ls ~148°) during the Phoenix mission; specific in-soil measurement campaigns on sols 46–47, 54–55, 69–71, 86, 98, 103–104, 111, 119, 122–124, and 149–150; additional flight data points used in prior recalibration from sols 86, 91, 103, 104, and 122 between 00:00 and 04:00
datasets.location_coverage: Phoenix landing site (68.2°N, 234.2°E); measurements in air at heights from 0 to ~2.2 m depending on robotic arm position; some comparisons note measurements at ~3 cm above ground and at 0.8 m height (sols 55–56)
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: Typically sampled at 1.2 s during ~30 min blocks a few times per sol; extended blocks ranging from ~30 min to ~20 hr were also taken
datasets.how_used: Primary in situ dataset analyzed: the authors apply a new recalibration/translation to Phoenix TECP flight-unit raw humidity output (DNRH) and board temperature (Tb) to derive recalibrated frost point, water vapor pressure, and RH; used to characterize diurnal/seasonal near-surface humidity at the Phoenix site and assess atmosphere–regolith exchange and brine-formation potential.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: MSL data used in Figures 9 and 10
datasets.measurement_observable: In situ relative humidity (RH) and temperature values used for comparison with Phoenix brine stability/day-night vapor pressure ratio analyses (Figures 9 and 10)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Used for nighttime values (~04:00–06:00) in day/night ratio comparison; figure labels indicate MSL, MY32 (Mars Year 32) for the comparison plot (Figure 9)
datasets.location_coverage: MSL landing site: 4.5°S, 37.4°E (Gale crater); values referenced at the ground and at 1.6 m height (Figure 10)
datasets.how_used: Comparative dataset: REMS humidity/temperature values are used to compare Phoenix vs. MSL day/night water vapor pressure ratios and to plot MSL environmental conditions against perchlorate deliquescence/eutectic stability curves in the brine-formation analysis (Figures 9–10).

output_parsed.paper_title: Relative Humidity on Mars: New Results From the Phoenix TECP Sensor

queries.query: Use Phoenix lander TECP atmospheric humidity sensor time-series to quantify the full-mission diurnal cycle of near-surface water vapor pressure and frost-point temperature (including the warm/dry midday regime versus predawn minima) to constrain polar atmosphere–regolith H2O exchange strength.

Assemble Phoenix lander Microscopy, Electrochemistry, and Conductivity Analyzer (MECA) TECP environmental measurements (raw humidity sensor output and electronics-board temperature with associated derived humidity metrics) during multi-hour robotic-arm activity blocks to test for short-lived near-surface saturation conditions relevant to transient brine-forming windows.

output_parsed.paper_title: Relative Humidity on Mars: New Results From the Phoenix TECP Sensor

queries.query: For the Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity rover at Gale crater, use Rover Environmental Monitoring Station reduced (RDR) meteorology in physical units to quantify predawn near-surface relative humidity and temperature (nominally 1.6 m height) for computing nighttime water vapor pressure and day/night vapor-pressure ratios during the early mission season (e.g., Mars Year 32).

Using Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity rover Rover Environmental Monitoring Station raw (EDR) engineering/telemetry outputs, evaluate low-temperature nighttime humidity-sensor behavior and reconstruct relative humidity and temperature time series suitable for cross-checking derived nighttime water vapor pressures at Gale crater without relying on higher-level processing assumptions.

final_output.query: Use Phoenix lander TECP atmospheric humidity sensor time-series to quantify the full-mission diurnal cycle of near-surface water vapor pressure and frost-point temperature (including the warm/dry midday regime versus predawn minima) to constrain polar atmosphere–regolith H2O exchange strength.

Assemble Phoenix lander Microscopy, Electrochemistry, and Conductivity Analyzer (MECA) TECP environmental measurements (raw humidity sensor output and electronics-board temperature with associated derived humidity metrics) during multi-hour robotic-arm activity blocks to test for short-lived near-surface saturation conditions relevant to transient brine-forming windows.

For the Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity rover at Gale crater, use Rover Environmental Monitoring Station reduced (RDR) meteorology in physical units to quantify predawn near-surface relative humidity and temperature (nominally 1.6 m height) for computing nighttime water vapor pressure and day/night vapor-pressure ratios during the early mission season (e.g., Mars Year 32).

Using Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity rover Rover Environmental Monitoring Station raw (EDR) engineering/telemetry outputs, evaluate low-temperature nighttime humidity-sensor behavior and reconstruct relative humidity and temperature time series suitable for cross-checking derived nighttime water vapor pressures at Gale crater without relying on higher-level processing assumptions.
